findings.title: Use of srand with time()
findings.trigger: Using the current time to seed the random number generator can predict the sequence of numbers generated.
findings.assumptions: The random numbers are used for a non-cryptographic purpose, and the security of the application does not rely on the unpredictability of the random numbers.

findings.title: Infinite Loop Potential
findings.trigger: If ability1.durationSeconds is set to a very large value or if the dummy's health is never reduced to zero, the loop could run indefinitely.
findings.assumptions: The durationSeconds is intended to be a reasonable value and the game logic ensures the dummy's health is reduced.

findings.title: Integer Overflow
findings.trigger: If damagePerTick is very large, the cast to int and subtraction from health could cause an integer overflow, leading to unexpected behavior or crashes.
findings.assumptions: damagePerTick values are reasonable and within expected ranges.

findings.title: Missing Logging of Ability 2 Usage
findings.trigger: The use of ability 2 is logged, but there is no similar logging for other potential game events or abilities, which could make debugging or monitoring more difficult.
findings.assumptions: Logging is not a security concern in this context, but it is a good practice for maintainability and debugging.
